answer: A decaying identity bond stops bulk fake identities. Each identity locks a 70-credit limestone tablet in a karst vault, where dripping water erodes it on a spiral schedule, losing 7 credits each epoch. A prism above the vault splits light across the tablet, and its spectrum publicly reads the remaining thickness for any auditor to recompute. Keeping 1,000 fakes alive costs 7,000 credits per epoch plus 70,000 locked; an honest agent tops up 7 once per epoch. A rented-top-up ring fails because each top-up is key-bound to one tablet.
